dominant_regions: Deccan Plateau: Telangana (Adilabad, Nizamabad, Khammam), Maharashtra (Vidarbha, Marathwada), Madhya Pradesh (Malwa, Nimar), Gujarat, Northern Karnataka.
characteristics_and_texture: Clay content 40-60% dominated by montmorillonite clay mineral; high swelling and shrinkage properties; forms wide deep cracks during dry season; self-ploughing; very high moisture retention capacity but poor internal drainage when wet.
major_nutrient_deficiencies: High in calcium and potassium; deficient in Nitrogen, Phosphorus, Zinc, and available Iron.
soil_amendments_and_reclamation: Incorporate broad-bed and furrow (BBF) land configuration to drain excess monsoon surface water. Apply Gypsum @ 1-2 tonnes/acre if exchangeable sodium percentage (ESP) exceeds 15% (sodic phase). Deep summer chiseling once in 3 years.
green_manuring_and_organic_practices: Incorporate Dhaincha (Sesbania aculeata) or Sunnhemp (Crotalaria juncea) at 45 DAS (adds 8-10 tonnes green biomass/acre). Apply FYM @ 5 tonnes/acre.

dominant_regions: Southern Telangana (Mahabubnagar, Nalgonda, Rangareddy), Andhra Pradesh (Rayalaseema), Tamil Nadu, Odisha, Chhota Nagpur plateau.
characteristics_and_texture: Formed by weathering of ancient granitic rocks; red color due to ferric oxides; light textured, sandy loam to sandy clay loam; high infiltration rate; low moisture retention capacity; prone to surface crusting after heavy rains.
major_nutrient_deficiencies: Deficient in Nitrogen, Phosphorus, Potassium, Calcium, Magnesium, and Zinc.
soil_amendments_and_reclamation: Break surface crusting using spike tooth harrow after rains. Apply tank silt @ 20-30 bullock cartloads (15 tonnes)/acre once in 4 years to enhance moisture retention and clay fraction. Ridge-furrow cultivation across slope.
green_manuring_and_organic_practices: Green manuring with Sunnhemp @ 15 kg seed/acre. Apply vermicompost @ 2 tonnes/acre or enriched FYM.

dominant_regions: Indo-Gangetic Plains: Punjab, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, West Bengal, coastal river deltas of Krishna, Godavari, Mahanadi, and Cauvery.
characteristics_and_texture: Deposited by Himalayan and peninsular river systems; loamy sand to silty clay loam; deep friable structure; excellent porosity and capillary conductivity; highly responsive to irrigation and intensive multi-cropping.
major_nutrient_deficiencies: Deficient in Nitrogen, Phosphorus, Zinc, and Manganese (especially in rice-wheat rotations).
soil_amendments_and_reclamation: Maintain balanced NPK stoichiometry (4:2:1 ratio). Laser land leveling to optimize water distribution and avoid localized waterlogging. Crop residue incorporation (Happy Seeder / Super Seeder technology).
green_manuring_and_organic_practices: Summer Green Mungbean / Dhaincha incorporation after wheat harvest. Inoculation with Trichoderma viride to accelerate stubble decomposition.

dominant_regions: Indo-Gangetic canal command areas (UP, Punjab, Haryana), canal irrigated pockets of Telangana and Karnataka, coastal tracts of Gujarat and AP.
characteristics_and_texture: High soluble salts (EC > 4.0 dS/m in saline soils) or high exchangeable sodium (ESP > 15%, SAR > 13, pH > 8.5 in sodic/alkali soils); soil particles disperse creating impermeable slickenside; severe drainage failure; white or black encrustation.
major_nutrient_deficiencies: Extreme deficiency of Zinc, Iron, and available Calcium; toxic accumulation of Sodium, Carbonates, and Boron.
soil_amendments_and_reclamation: Compute Gypsum Requirement (GR). Apply agricultural grade Gypsum (CaSO4·2H2O @ 70-80% purity) @ 3-5 tonnes/acre broadcast and mixed in top 10 cm soil, followed by impounding 10-15 cm water for 15 days to leach displaced sodium down drains. Provide subsurface tile drainage.
green_manuring_and_organic_practices: Grow Dhaincha (Sesbania aculeata) tolerant to pH up to 9.5; incorporate at 45 DAS (releases carbonic acid during decomposition which neutralizes sodicity). Apply press mud @ 5 tonnes/acre.
citation: ICAR-CSSRI Karnal Reclamation of Sodic Soils Handbook 2025

dominant_regions: High rainfall hilly zones: North-Eastern States, Kerala, Coastal Karnataka, Konkan Maharashtra, Chhota Nagpur plateau of Jharkhand and Odisha.
characteristics_and_texture: Intense tropical leaching removes basic cations (Ca, Mg, K, Na); dominated by kaolinite clay and iron/aluminium oxides; high phosphorus fixation capacity (P gets locked as insoluble aluminium and iron phosphates).
major_nutrient_deficiencies: Severe deficiency of Phosphorus, Calcium, Magnesium, Boron, and Molybdenum; Aluminium and Manganese toxicity.
soil_amendments_and_reclamation: Liming: Apply agricultural limestone (CaCO3) or dolomite (CaCO3·MgCO3) @ 1.0 - 2.5 tonnes/acre based on soil buffer capacity once in 3 years. Apply Rock Phosphate (RP) instead of water-soluble SSP, as acid soil naturally dissolves rock phosphate.
green_manuring_and_organic_practices: Apply well-rotted FYM @ 5 tonnes/acre + biofertilizers (Phosphate Solubilizing Fungi like Aspergillus awamori).
citation: ICAR-IISS Bhopal Acid Soil Amelioration Guide 2025

dominant_regions: Western Ghats, Coastal Kerala, Karnataka, Ratnagiri (Maharashtra), parts of Odisha and West Bengal.
characteristics_and_texture: Coarse, porous, honey-combed structure rich in iron and aluminium sesquioxides; poor nutrient holding capacity; low cation exchange capacity (CEC); rapid organic matter oxidation.
major_nutrient_deficiencies: Deficient in Potassium, Calcium, Magnesium, Boron, and available Phosphorus.
soil_amendments_and_reclamation: Split application of chemical fertilizers to avoid leaching loss. Apply Dolomite @ 500 kg/acre to replenish Calcium and Magnesium. Mulching to protect surface from heavy rainfall erosion.
green_manuring_and_organic_practices: Intercropping with velvet bean (Mucuna pruriens) or cowpea. Application of coir pith compost @ 3 tonnes/acre.

dominant_regions: Sundarbans (West Bengal), Coastal Odisha, Andhra Pradesh (Krishna-Godavari delta coastal fringe), Tamil Nadu, Gujarat (Rann of Kutch).
characteristics_and_texture: Periodic sea water inundation and high shallow saline groundwater table; high electrical conductivity (EC > 8.0 dS/m); heavy clay to silty loam texture with poor aeration.
major_nutrient_deficiencies: High in Sodium and Chlorides; low in Nitrogen and Zinc.
soil_amendments_and_reclamation: Construct perimeter bunds with one-way flap sluice gates to prevent tidal ingress. Raised-bed and sunken-furrow system (grow paddy in furrows and vegetables on raised beds). Leaching with fresh rainwater during monsoon.
green_manuring_and_organic_practices: Cultivate salt-tolerant halophytic green manures; incorporate organic paddy straw mulch to suppress capillary salt ascent during dry summer months.
citation: ICAR-CSSRI Regional Research Station Canning Town 2025

dominant_regions: Northern Bihar, Saurashtra (Gujarat), parts of Western Rajasthan, Rayalaseema (AP), and Belgaum (Karnataka).
characteristics_and_texture: Contain free calcium carbonate (CaCO3 > 5% to 20%) in form of soft powdery lime or hard nodules (kankar); high buffering capacity; causes precipitation of phosphate and micronutrients.
major_nutrient_deficiencies: Severe fixation of Phosphorus; acute Iron deficiency (lime-induced iron chlorosis) and Zinc deficiency.
soil_amendments_and_reclamation: Band placement of phosphatic fertilizers with acidic fertilizers like Ammonium Sulphate instead of Urea. Apply elemental sulphur @ 200 kg/acre to create localized acidic micro-zones.
green_manuring_and_organic_practices: Incorporate green manure crops; application of press mud cake (PMC) @ 5 tonnes/acre which produces organic acids upon rotting.

dominant_regions: Western Rajasthan (Thar Desert: Jodhpur, Barmer, Bikaner, Jaisalmer), South-Western Punjab, Haryana fringe.
characteristics_and_texture: Coarse sand (>85% sand fraction); single-grain structure; excessive permeability; very poor water retention capacity (wilting point reached in 2-3 days); prone to severe wind erosion.
major_nutrient_deficiencies: Deficient in Nitrogen, Phosphorus, Potassium, Zinc, and Copper.
soil_amendments_and_reclamation: Shelterbelts and windbreaks using Acacia tortilis and Prosopis cineraria (Khejri). Compaction of sandy subsoil with heavy rollers to reduce percolation loss. Drip irrigation with fertigation mandatory.
green_manuring_and_organic_practices: Incorporate Guar (Cluster bean) @ 15 kg/acre. Application of Bentonite clay @ 4 tonnes/acre in root zone to improve water holding capacity.

dominant_regions: Telangana (Warangal, Karimnagar), Maharashtra (Western plains), MP (Indore, Ujjain), Karnataka (Dharwad).
characteristics_and_texture: Depth 50-100 cm; clay content 35-45%; dark brown to black; good balance of drainage and moisture retention compared to deep heavy vertisols; versatile for two-crop rotations (Soybean-Wheat or Cotton-Pulse).
major_nutrient_deficiencies: Deficient in Nitrogen, Phosphorus, Sulphur, and Zinc.
soil_amendments_and_reclamation: Contour bunding and vegetative barriers (Vetiver grass hedgerows) to arrest soil erosion. Regular addition of FYM.
green_manuring_and_organic_practices: Intercropping with Pigeonpea / Cowpea; green leaf manuring with Subabul (Leucaena leucocephala) loppings.

soil_type: Peaty and Marshy Soils (Kari Soils / Histosols)
dominant_regions: Kottayam and Alappuzha districts of Kerala (Kuttanad submerged tracts), coastal Odisha, Sundarbans.
characteristics_and_texture: Formed under anaerobic waterlogged conditions; dark black color; spongy consistency; very high accumulation of undecomposed organic matter; contains iron pyrite (FeS2) which oxidizes to sulphuric acid on drainage producing acid sulphate conditions.
major_nutrient_deficiencies: Low available Phosphorus; Potassium and Copper deficiency; Iron and Aluminium toxicity.
soil_amendments_and_reclamation: Subsurface drainage with controlled water table management. Heavy liming using burnt quicklime (CaO) or hydrated lime @ 2-3 tonnes/acre to neutralize acidity.
green_manuring_and_organic_practices: Application of wood ash @ 1 tonne/acre to supply potash and neutralize acidity. Balanced biofertilizers.
citation: KAU Regional Agricultural Research Station Kumarakom 2025

dominant_regions: Himalayan foothills: Jammu & Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Nilgiris (Tamil Nadu).
characteristics_and_texture: Formed under temperate forest cover; loam to sandy loam texture with stones and pebbles; high gravel content; shallow to medium depth on steep slopes.
major_nutrient_deficiencies: Deficient in Phosphorus, Zinc, and Boron.
soil_amendments_and_reclamation: Bench terracing, contour trenching, and inward sloping terraces with vegetative grassed waterways to eliminate slope run-off erosion. Mulching with pine needles or oak leaves.
green_manuring_and_organic_practices: Incorporation of white clover (Trifolium repens) as cover crop; application of well-cured sheep manure or compost @ 5 tonnes/acre.
